`ScrollArea.test.ts` tests the attributes and the `element` slot of the content, the measurement when it resizes, and its error outside a viewport.
`ScrollArea.test.ts` tests `aria-hidden` of the corner, the value of the developer, and the size of the corner.
`ScrollArea.test.ts` tests the measurement, the overflow attributes, the thresholds, the variables, the thumb length, `scrolling` and right-to-left.

exceptions.title: shows scrollbars after mount compute before the first ResizeObserver measurement
exceptions.reason: The case replaces the observer with one that reports nothing. A real observer reports in the first frame, before the paint, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (`test/measurements/scroll-area.test.ts`). The parts measure nothing by hand at the mount.

exceptions.title: recomputes horizontal overflow edges when direction changes
exceptions.reason: The direction changes with no event. A part handles the events that the browser sends, and reads the direction at the next measurement.
`ScrollArea.pointer.test.ts` tests the press on the track, `mousedown`, the wheel and the thumb that fills its track. `ScrollArea.test.ts` tests `aria-hidden`, the orientation and the `element` slot.

`hovering` is cut. CSS `:hover` of the root gives the same hook: `.ScrollArea:hover .Scrollbar`, in `@media (hover: hover)`. The browser owns this state, also for a pointer that is over the root at the mount, for a touch, and during a drag with the pointer outside the root.

exceptions.title: ignores thumb clicks when the native path differs from the synthetic target
exceptions.reason: The case tests the target of a React synthetic event. A press on the thumb reaches the listener of the thumb first, and the press is then in progress when the track gets the event.
`ScrollArea.pointer.test.ts` tests the drag in each direction, the end of a press, a second pointer, another button, scroll snap and an unmount during a press.

exceptions.title: ends a drag whose release was missed instead of scrolling on hover
exceptions.reason: The case stubs the capture functions to make a release that never comes. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit send the release and `lostpointercapture` to the thumb, also with `display: none` (`test/measurements/scroll-area.test.ts`).

exceptions.title: lets a new pointer take over when capture was silently dropped
exceptions.reason: The case stubs the capture functions to drop the capture with no event. The browsers send `lostpointercapture` when the thumb loses the capture (`test/measurements/scroll-area.test.ts`).
`ScrollArea.test.ts` tests the tab stop, the overflow attributes, the rubber band of WebKit, the animations, `scrolling` and the errors of the viewport.

exceptions.title: releases a completed animation target while another animation is paused
exceptions.reason: The viewport keeps no list of animations. Each animation that runs one task after the mount measures when it ends.
CSS `:hover` of the root gives the same hook, so the state has no `hovering`, and the scrollbar has no `data-hovering`.
`ScrollAreaCornerState` holds no field, so the corner gives no `state` and no state type.
